new_candidates.body:
### Is there an already existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues (searched for `TypeLookupManager`, `TypeLookupRequestListener`, `stop_request_processor_thread`, `dds.tls.requests`; #5273 fixes a leak in the same destructor but not the ordering; #3303 is a different reader-listener race).

### Expected behavior

Deleting a `DomainParticipant` while a remote participant is sending `TypeLookup_getTypeDependencies` requests to it must not crash. `TypeLookupManager::~TypeLookupManager()` should stop (and join) the request-processing thread **before** it deletes the builtin reply writer and its `WriterHistory`, so that an in-flight `answer_request()` can never touch freed memory.

### Current behavior

Rare SIGSEGV in the TypeLookup request thread (`dds.tls.requests`) while the main thread is deleting the participant. Stack of the crashing thread (symbols from the ROS 2 Lyrical binary of Fast DDS 3.6.2):

```
TypeLookupRequestListener::process_requests
  -> TypeLookupRequestListener::check_get_type_dependencies_request
  -> TypeLookupRequestListener::answer_request
  -> TypeLookupManager::send(TypeLookup_Reply&)          // send_impl(..., builtin_reply_writer_history_)
  -> WriterHistory::create_change
  -> pthread_mutex_lock                                  // SIGSEGV: history already deleted
```

Main thread at the same time: `DomainParticipant` deletion (reached via ROS 2 `rmw_destroy_node` -> participant destruction when the last node of the context is destroyed) -> `TypeLookupManager::~TypeLookupManager`.

The destructor order in `src/cpp/fastdds/builtin/type_lookup_service/TypeLookupManager.cpp` (v3.6.2, identical on `master` at 7dd4b4d17f) is:

```cpp
TypeLookupManager::~TypeLookupManager()
{
    // 1. remove builtin endpoints
    participant_->deleteUserEndpoint(builtin_reply_writer_->getGuid());   // ...
    // 2. delete histories
    delete builtin_request_writer_history_;
    delete builtin_reply_writer_history_;                                  // <- used by send(TypeLookup_Reply&)
    ...
    // 3. only now stop the request thread
    delete reply_listener_;
    delete request_listener_;   // ~TypeLookupRequestListener -> stop_request_processor_thread() -> join
```

Between steps 1-2 and step 3 the `request_processor_thread` is still running and may be inside `answer_request()`, which calls `typelookup_manager_->send(reply)` -> `send_impl(reply, &reply_type_, builtin_reply_writer_history_)` on a deleted history (and a deleted writer). The window is narrow, which is why this shows up as a flaky crash under load rather than deterministically.

### Steps to reproduce

The race is timing dependent; we observed it once in CI (Ubuntu 26.04, many ROS 2 test processes starting in parallel in the same domain) and could not reproduce it deterministically in ~9 minutes of stress (3 processes creating/deleting ~4100 participants with 12 types while 4 loops kept spawning fresh processes that issue `getTypeDependencies` requests). The report is therefore based on the stack trace plus code reading. Suggested set-up to widen the window:

1. Process A: create a participant with a DataWriter whose type has dependencies (so remote participants need `getTypeDependencies`), then delete the participant in a loop.
2. Processes B..N: continuously start, discover A, request its type dependencies (any new participant that sees an unknown type does this automatically), and exit.
3. Optionally add a sleep inside `TypeLookupRequestListener::answer_request()` between the request dequeue and `typelookup_manager_->send()` to make the window deterministic; the crash then reproduces every time A deletes its participant while a request is being answered.

Proposed fix: in `~TypeLookupManager()` call `request_listener_->stop_request_processor_thread()` (and delete `request_listener_`) **before** `deleteUserEndpoint(...)`/`delete *_history_`, or at least before the reply writer and `builtin_reply_writer_history_` are destroyed.

### Fast DDS version/commit

v3.6.2 (ROS 2 Lyrical binary `ros-lyrical-fastdds 3.6.2`). The destructor is unchanged on `master` as of 2026-10-28 (last commit touching the file: 7dd4b4d17f).

### Platform/Architecture

Ubuntu 26.04 amd64 (closest Tier 1 entry: Ubuntu Noble amd64; the affected code is platform independent)

### Transport layer

Default configuration (UDPv4 & SHM)

### Additional context

- Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS x86_64, gcc 15.2.0, ROS 2 Lyrical, rmw_fastrtps_cpp 9.4.10.
- In ROS 2 the participant is deleted when the last node of a context is destroyed (rmw_fastrtps `decrement_context_impl_ref_count`), so any test suite that creates and destroys one node per test performs many participant deletions while sibling test processes are discovering it, which is how we hit it.
- Workaround on our side: keep one long-lived node per test module so the participant is deleted only once.

### XML configuration file

```
Not applicable (default profiles; only environment variables RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_fastrtps_cpp and ROS_DOMAIN_ID were set).
```

### Relevant log output

```
Thread (dds.tls.requests) received signal SIGSEGV
#0 pthread_mutex_lock
#1 eprosima::fastdds::rtps::WriterHistory::create_change
#2 eprosima::fastdds::dds::builtin::TypeLookupManager::send(eprosima::fastdds::dds::builtin::TypeLookup_Reply&) const
#3 eprosima::fastdds::dds::builtin::TypeLookupRequestListener::answer_request
#4 eprosima::fastdds::dds::builtin::TypeLookupRequestListener::check_get_type_dependencies_request
#5 eprosima::fastdds::dds::builtin::TypeLookupRequestListener::process_requests
Main thread: rclpy node.destroy_node() -> rmw_destroy_node -> participant deletion -> TypeLookupManager::~TypeLookupManager
```

### Network traffic capture

```
Not available (CI run).
```

new_candidates.body:
## Bug report

**Required Info:**

- Operating System: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x86_64), Python 3.14.4
- Installation type: binaries (`ros-lyrical-rclpy 10.0.11`)
- Version or commit hash: rclpy 10.0.11; the same code is on `lyrical` (02b36e689a) and `rolling` (501ed6cc97, `rclpy/rclpy/context.py` lines 150-154)
- DDS implementation: rmw_fastrtps_cpp 9.4.10 (not relevant, the bug is in pure Python)
- Client library (if applicable): rclpy

#### Steps to reproduce issue

```python
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node

rclpy.init()
nodes = [Node(f'n{i}') for i in range(4)]
rclpy.shutdown()  # Context._cleanup should destroy every tracked node

def alive(n):
    try:
        n.get_name()
        return True
    except Exception:  # InvalidHandle once destroy_node() ran
        return False

print('alive after shutdown:', [alive(n) for n in nodes])
```

#### Expected behavior

`Context.shutdown()` / `rclpy.shutdown()` destroys every node tracked by the context (that is the documented purpose of `track_node`: "When the Context is destroyed, it will destroy every BaseNode it tracks").

```
alive after shutdown: [False, False, False, False]
```

#### Actual behavior

Every second tracked node is skipped:

```
alive after shutdown: [False, True, False, True]
```

With 2 nodes the second one survives, with 3 nodes the middle one survives, and so on. The surviving nodes keep their `rcl_node_t` (and the rmw/DDS resources behind it) until garbage collection or until the user calls `destroy_node()` explicitly after shutdown.

#### Additional information

Root cause is a mutate-while-iterating bug in `Context._cleanup`:

```python
def _cleanup(self) -> None:
    for weak_node in self.__node_weak_ref_list:
        node = weak_node()
        if node is not None:
            node.destroy_node()
```

`BaseNode.destroy_node()` first calls `self.context.untrack_node(self)`, which does `del self.__node_weak_ref_list[found_index]` on the very list being iterated. The list shrinks under the `for` loop, so the element right after the one just destroyed is skipped.

A minimal fix is to iterate over a snapshot (`for weak_node in list(self.__node_weak_ref_list):`) or to pop from the list until it is empty. Happy to open a PR if that is welcome.

Impact seen in practice: multi-node test processes that rely on `rclpy.shutdown()` for cleanup leak nodes/participants (we hit "Too many open files"-style failures in CI before adding explicit `destroy_node()` calls everywhere).
new_candidates.title: Context._cleanup skips every second tracked node on shutdown (mutating __node_weak_ref_list while iterating)
